# markdown-s2 — Safe Markdown → HTML renderer (tier S2) ## Module: `src/markdown.js` (ES module) - `export function render(markdown: string, { headingIds = false } = {}): string` → HTML. - `export function toc(markdown: string): Array<{ level: number, text: string, slug: string }>` — every ATX/setext heading in document order; `text` is the heading's plain text (inline markup removed). - `export function slugify(text: string, seen?: Map)` — GitHub-style slug: lower-case; remove every character that is not a letter, digit, space, `-` or `_`; spaces → `-`. When a `Map` of previously seen slugs is passed, repeated slugs get `-1`, `-2`, … suffixes. `toc` and `headingIds` use one map per document. ## Output conventions Follow CommonMark 0.31 HTML output (as produced by the reference implementation commonmark.js) plus GFM tables and strikethrough, except where this spec says otherwise. Insignificant whitespace between block-level tags is not significant to the tests; `
`/`
`, `
`/`
`, ``/`` are equivalent; table alignment may be expressed as `align="left"` or `style="text-align:left"`. Required features: - ATX headings `#`…`######` (closing `#`s stripped), setext headings (`===`, `---`). With `headingIds: true`, headings get `id=""`: `

My title

`. - Paragraphs; soft line breaks preserved as `\n`; hard breaks via two trailing spaces or a trailing backslash → `
`. - Emphasis/strong with `*` and `_` (CommonMark rules incl. no intraword `_` emphasis), `***x***` → `x`; GFM `~~strike~~` → ``. - Code spans (multi-backtick delimiters, one leading/trailing space stripped when both present). - Fenced code blocks (``` and ~~~, info string → `class="language-"`) and indented code blocks. - Blockquotes (nested, with lazy continuation lines), thematic breaks (`---`, `***`, `___`). - Bullet lists (`-`, `*`, `+`) and ordered lists (`1.` / `1)`, `start` attribute when not 1), nesting by indentation, tight vs loose lists (`

  • ` when loose). - Inline links `[t](url "title")`, images `![alt](src "title")`, reference links `[t][ref]`, `[ref]` with definitions `[ref]: url "title"` (case-insensitive labels), autolinks `` and `<>` (→ `mailto:`). - Backslash escapes; HTML-escape `& < > "` in text, attributes and code. - GFM pipe tables with header row, delimiter row, optional alignment (`:--`, `:-:`, `--:`), inline markup in cells, `\|` escapes. ## Safety (deliberate deviation from CommonMark) - Raw HTML (block and inline) is NOT passed through: it is rendered as escaped text, e.g. `` → `

    <script>x</script>

content.text:
I've built the renderer, but I couldn't run any of it. The auto-mode permission check blocked every command that loads the vendored code ("Code from External"), including the required `node --test`. So the public smoke tests and my own sample inputs have not been run, and I can't say the implementation passes. **Built so far (reuse-first, no runtime dependencies):** - **Search and copy:** I searched GitHub in the browser, chose `markedjs/marked` (MIT, has GFM tables and strikethrough), and copied the whole `marked@15.0.12/lib/marked.esm.js` through the browser into `src/vendor/marked.esm.js`. - **Changes to the copied code:** - Raw HTML is no longer recognised, as blocks or inline. It falls through as text and is escaped, so `` becomes `

<script>x</script>

`. - HTML no longer interrupts paragraphs, tables, setext headings or list items. - Only `& < > "` are escaped, so `'` is left alone. - GFM task lists and bare-URL autolinks are off, so output stays close to CommonMark plus tables and strikethrough. - **`src/markdown.js` (new glue code):** - `render`, `toc` and `slugify`. `slugify` follows GitHub's rules, with `-1`, `-2`, … suffixes for repeats, using one map per document. - `headingIds` adds the slug as the heading's `id`. - Output adjusted to CommonMark style (`
`, `
`, ``, `language-` code classes). - Link and image URLs are percent-encoded, and `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:` and non-image `data:` URLs are replaced with `#`. - Numeric entities and a short list of common named ones are decoded. Named entities not on that list are left unchanged. - **`src/cli.js`:** supports ``, `--toc` and `--ids`. - **Records:** `PROVENANCE.json` and `src/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` hold the source, the full MIT licence text and every change. **Why it was blocked and what I did instead:** the check refuses to execute code downloaded from the internet. I searched the vendored file for `import`, `require`, `eval`, `fetch`, `process`, `fs` and similar, and found nothing; it is a pure string parser. I then tried `node --test` once and it was denied too, so I stopped rather than look for a way around the check. **To finish:** allow `node` to run in this workspace (for example, a Bash permission rule for `node --test` and `node src/*`). Then I can run the smoke tests and fix whatever they turn up.
